reading.body:
K-Motion Interactive is a sports motion-capture company in Scottsdale, not a data center, and contributes zero megawatts to Arizona's compute capacity.

The entry came from a mistagged OpenStreetMap point. The stored coordinates resolve to a different small business in the McDowell Mountain Business Park, a multi-tenant office and light-industrial park. No server rooms, colocation space, or dedicated data center infrastructure exist at that address. The company itself makes 3D biomechanics analysis systems for golf and baseball swing instruction.

This matters for AI because capacity inventories are only as good as their tagging. Arizona has 56 mapped facilities, of which 4 publish power figures totaling 512 MW. A mistagged point inflates the count of sites without adding a single megawatt, and the error is invisible unless someone checks the address. The same batch of nine rows spans Phoenix, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, and Scottsdale, so these are not one shared building but nine independently mistagged small businesses across the metro.

What the data does not show is how many other entries carry the same defect. It covers one facility, its coordinates, and its current occupant. It says nothing about whether the other 55 Arizona sites were verified, and it publishes no power figure for this one because there is none to publish.
